artworks.title: Great American Shrike or Butcher Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of four birds perched on branches with red berries. The birds are illustrated with fine details, showing their distinct coloration of grey, white, and black feathers. They are depicted in various poses: one is perched upright, while others are positioned in more dynamic stances, interacting with the branches and berries. The leaves are a lush green with visible veins. The branches curve smoothly, supporting the birds and clusters of red berries.

artworks.title: Lincoln Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two finches among foliage. The image features two finches, one perched on a branch and the other on the ground, surrounded by detailed illustrations of plants and flowers. The branch holds small, delicate pink flowers with open petals, while the ground is covered with a lush layer of large green leaves and white flowers. The composition captures the beauty and detail of the natural environment, focusing on the intricacies of both the birds and the surrounding flora.

artworks.title: Canadian Titmouse
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on a leafy branch with red berries. The birds have detailed plumage, with a combination of brown, black, and white colors. One bird is shown feeding the young bird below it, while the third bird is perched higher on the branch.

artworks.title: Ruby-crowned Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds are perched on a branch surrounded by pink flowers and green leaves. The color palette includes shades of green, pink, and brown in the branch, leaves, and flowers. The birds display yellow, black, and gray feathers, with a red crown on their heads. The branch, centrally positioned, extends upwards, with pink flowers around the top half, and one bird is to the right while the other is to the lower left.

artworks.title: Labrador Falcon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two falcons perched on branches. The upper falcon is slightly hunched with dark plumage and an intense gaze, while the lower falcon has its wings partially spread and is vocalizing, with detailed plumage showing intricate patterns. Both falcons have sharp talons gripping the branches they are perched upon. The painting captures the form and details of these birds against a light background.

artworks.title: American Crossbill
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Several birds are perched on and hanging from leafy branches. The color palette features mixes of greens, browns, reds, and greys, with vibrant green foliage. In the upper part of the image, two birds sit closely near the branches. Below them, other birds with varying patterns of grey, brown, and white plumage are positioned at different angles, some hanging upside down, around the middle of the composition. On the lower right, a bird with reddish tones stands out against lighter leaves.

artworks.title: Brown-headed Worm-eating Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: In the painting, a bird is perched on a branch surrounded by orange flowers and green leaves. Two butterflies are also present, one with blue and black wings and the other with eye-patterned brown wings. The artwork is done in the style of John James Audubon and combines detailed botanical and ornithological elements against a plain background.

artworks.title: Little Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is an illustration of two Little Owls. One owl is perched on a branch, while the other is on a rock holding a mouse. The owls are depicted with detailed brown and white feather patterns, sharp beaks, yellow eyes, and dynamic poses. The background includes grass and rocks. The artwork showcases a high level of realism and attention to detail. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Shore Lark
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts four birds with intricate plumage, standing near thick, green foliage. The birds display shades of brown, white, black, and cream, set against a backdrop of rich green vegetation and earthy tones. From left to right, two birds are resting on the foliage, one looking sideways while the other two are in a downward-facing position, with the last bird peering into the scene from the edge of the image.

artworks.title: Canada Goose
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: Red-throated Diver
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting red-throated divers in a natural setting. Three birds are shown near water, surrounded by aquatic plants and rocks, with varying postures and plumages. The largest bird stands on a rock with a black and white feather pattern and a red throat. One bird is in water with wings poised, and another bird is near greenery. Lily-like flowers are visible in the background, adding color to the scene. The artwork showcases detailed anatomical features and textures of the birds.

artworks.title: Fresh Water Marsh Hen
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds among reeds. The painting depicts two birds, known as Fresh Water Marsh Hens, within a cluster of tall, green, and yellow reeds. The foreground bird has vibrant plumage with shades of brown, orange, and subtle pinks, emphasizing its feathers. The background bird, rendered with similar finesse, adds depth to the composition. The pale blue water at the bottom contrasts with the earthy and green tones. The reeds subtly arch and intertwine, framing the birds. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Salt Water Marsh Hen
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds standing on marshy ground among tall grasses. One bird is larger and standing erect with its beak open, while the smaller bird is leaning forward. The birds are detailed with intricate plumage and distinct coloration. The scene captures a natural wetland habitat, with water and reeds in the background, typical of a marsh environment. The focus is on realism and naturalism.

artworks.title: Virginia Rail
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of Virginia Rails in their natural habitat. The artwork shows three Virginia Rails - a male, a female, and a young bird - in a marsh environment with green reeds and water. The birds have detailed plumage in shades of brown, rust, and gray. They are captured in naturalistic poses - one standing, one calling, and the other resting. The surroundings highlight the water and plant life of the habitat. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Summer or Wood Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of wood ducks. The image features a group of wood ducks among leafy branches. Two ducks are perched on a branch, facing each other. Their plumage displays colors such as blues, greens, browns, and whites. Below, another duck is shown with wings spread. To the right, another duck is nestled in what seems to be a nest or hollow, looking outward. Detailed leaves frame the group, creating a naturalistic setting for the birds.

artworks.title: Booby Gannet
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a branch overlooking a body of water with a settlement in the distance. The bird is depicted in profile with detailed plumage, showcasing dark brown feathers mixed with white on its underbelly. Its long beak is open, displaying its sharp, pinkish-yellow bill. It is standing on a branch with webbed feet, which are pale yellow. The background features a calm blue expanse of water leading to a small town with buildings and a few anchored boats, set against a sky dotted with clouds.

artworks.title: Esquimaux Curlew
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds in a natural setting. It features two illustrations of birds, one standing with a slightly downward stance and the other lying down. The bird standing upright has a long, slender beak and intricate brown and black feather patterns covering its body. The wings are detailed with a mix of browns, and the legs are slender and blue. The other bird, lying down, displays a lighter combination of feathers moving from pale bands on the underside to darker shades on the wings. The background shows a lush, textured landscape with varying shades of green suggesting grass and bushes.

artworks.title: Wilson's Plover
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is an image of two plovers by the water. It shows two plover birds standing by the edge of a body of water, one on a rocky surface and the other in the water. The birds have brown and white plumage and are shown in profile. The background includes the sea and minimal foliage. The image emphasizes the form and detail of the birds.

artworks.title: Least Bittern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds among tall grass. The artwork depicts three Least Bittern birds in a natural setting. The birds are shown with their long necks and extended beaks. The background consists of lush green tall grass. The intricate detailing of the feathers, the texture of the grass, and the posture of the birds capture a moment of stillness. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Great blue Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a detailed print of a great blue heron standing at the water's edge with its beak pointed downward. The heron is standing on brown ground and is surrounded by tall, pale-green grass. Its plumage exhibits a mix of blues, grays, and whites, with a splash of reddish orange on its leg and the top of its wing. The bird's elongated neck is bent down, and its yellow beak is open. Its wings are not fully extended, but they are raised upwards. It faces the left, and its head is in profile, with its eye looking out at us. The background behind the bird is blank, off-white paper.

artworks.title: Hyperborean Phalarope
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds in and around water. The painting depicts three phalaropes in different poses: one in flight, one resting in shallow water, and one standing on vegetation. The birds are colored with red necks, white, black, and gray tones. The background shows a watery landscape. The focus is on the grace and beauty of the birds with detailed feathers and background. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Wood Ibis
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a painting of a wood stork near the water. The wood stork has a long curved beak, detailed feathers, and elongated legs. There are trees, a cloudy sky, and other birds on the water's surface in the background. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed ornithological illustrations.

artworks.title: Louisiana Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: An ocean-blue bird with a long body and a flax-yellow beak and legs stands in a lush landscape in this vertical color print. The image is printed on cream-colored paper with a wide margin around the edges. The bird stands with its body in profile facing our left on a low dirt mound. Its head is turned completely around to our right with its beak tilted down and one amber-yellow eye looking our way. Its tall legs are dotted with brown, and a long blue and brown plume drapes down from its back. Long, plum-purple feathers adorn its throat, and white feathers line the underside of its neck and head. The bird stands next to a tall plant to the right. Bare tree trunks float in a pewter-gray river that begins in the lower left and widens as it reaches the center. The river divides the bird from a grove of palm trees, bushes, and reeds painted in muted tones of green, yellow, and gray that almost fills the left side. Another grove of palms in tones of gray fills the center distance with bare, contorted tree trunks in the water before it. The print is inscribed outside the image in all four corners and the bottom center. The upper left reads, “No. 44” and the upper right reads, “Plate CCXVII.” The lower left reads, “Drawn from Nature by J.J. Audubon. F.R.S. F.L.S.” and the lower right reads, “Engraved, Printed & Coloured by R. Havell, 1834.” The center inscription reads, “Louisiana Heron” printed in script and continues, “ARDEA LUDOVICIANA. Wils Male adult.”

artworks.title: Foolish Guillemot
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds on a rocky shoreline. The image shows two birds with sleek dark brown heads, white underparts, and darker wings and back. One bird appears to be sitting sedately, while the other has its head tilted back, with its beak open. They are depicted on rocky outcroppings by a choppy blue-green sea. The style emphasizes detailed and lifelike coloring to highlight the texture and plumage of the birds. This is in the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed and scientific illustrations of birds.
